references.text: Jesus calls his generation 'faithless and twisted,' reflecting Deuteronomy's description of a 'twisted and crooked generation.'
Paul uses the phrase 'a twisted and perverse generation' as a direct allusion to Moses' words about Israel's corrupt generation.
Proverbs describes those who leave the paths of righteousness to walk in darkness, echoing the twisted and crooked generation.
Isaiah portrays Israel as a sinful people, a guilty race, offspring of evildoers and corrupt children—similar language regarding moral corruption.
Peter urges his listeners to be saved from this twisted generation, directly alluding to Moses' description.
Later in the same song, Moses describes them as 'children without faithfulness,' reinforcing the theme of Israel's unfaithfulness.
The psalm warns against becoming like their fathers, a stubborn and rebellious generation with hearts not faithful to God.
